Need to test whether policy demand is durable across administrations or dependent on one election cycle, emergency stockpiling action, or temporary waiver regime.

memory_update.text: Politics should remain decomposed into policy-created demand and regulation-created constraints; the investable lanes are defense capacity, strategic minerals, compliance infrastructure, government IT, and public infrastructure rather than election sentiment alone.
Energetics and solid-rocket-motor inputs are the highest-priority Layer 1 chokepoint lane, with NEU, KRMN, and PKE as underfollowed candidates and LHX/NOC as reference anchors.
Strategic minerals should be scored by qualification, compliant feedstock, processing capacity, and funded procurement rather than mine ownership alone.
Tariff, customs, testing, certification, and supply-chain-visibility software/services are a second-order politics lane that needs more primary-source candidate discovery.
Before Layer 2, candidate validation must check primary contract records, obligated dollars, SEC filings, backlog, customer concentration, pricing structure, market cap, liquidity, and valuation.

The current universe has strong defense-industrial-base coverage but remains narrower in customs compliance, testing/certification, government IT subcontractors, and grid/power infrastructure beneficiaries.

summary: Layer 1C merges the Politics theme into an initial Serenity universe focused on policy-created demand and regulation-created bottlenecks rather than election narrative alone. The highest-priority clusters are defense industrial-base sub-tier capacity, energetics and solid-rocket-motor inputs, strategic minerals and rare-earth qualification, tariff/localization/supply-chain compliance infrastructure, government IT/data modernization, and publicly funded grid/power infrastructure. The universe deliberately uses large defense primes as reference leaders while prioritizing underfollowed or second-order public names where exposure may be hidden inside specialty chemicals, niche aerospace components, strategic materials, testing/compliance, or infrastructure services. Scores reflect Layer 1 Serenity relevance only and are not buy/sell recommendations.
